summary: Reproduced that current LPM ordering has no aging input, then added an opt-in --lpm-aging-tokens-per-pass setting. Active LPM passes now increase a per-request counter and the sort key combines matched-prefix tokens with the aging bonus. The default zero path retains the original sort key, temporarily deprioritized requests remain last, and the existing >128-request FCFS fallback does not accumulate LPM age.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the prepared source lacked the server argument, policy constructor input, and aging-aware sort API. Raw output: reports/j-4070812353a4/raw/failing-before.txt

17 tests plus 2 subtests passed, covering repeated hot-arrival displacement, exact-threshold stability, disabled behavior, temporary deprioritization, the 129-request FCFS boundary, CLI wiring, and adjacent scheduler policies. Raw output: reports/j-4070812353a4/raw/passing-after-unit-expanded.txt
The registered test file ran directly through its CI entry point: 7 tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-4070812353a4/raw/passing-after-direct.txt
All applicable repository formatting, lint, syntax, security, and registered-test checks passed. Raw output: reports/j-4070812353a4/raw/pre-commit.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The reproduced defect and regression are CPU-only Python scheduling decisions; no kernel or model execution participates in the LPM sort key. The assigned gfx950 was therefore not used as irrelevant evidence.

remaining_limitations: The production GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 8xB300 workload and its 20-60 second TTFT tail were not reproduced; that hardware, topology, traffic, and model weights were unavailable and a tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify them.
The regression deterministically validates queue ordering and the starvation bound in scheduler passes, not wall-clock TTFT under a full serving workload.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
